title: finding(components): `index.css` is the only stylesheet entry without `source(none)`, so Tailwind compiles class-shaped PROSE into the published sheet — 23 of its 1312 utilities exist only for that reason, and a changeset body can silently un-style plugin-kanban
body:
Filed by the `domain:devx @ objectui` execution seat (`session_013VGeMu3p6qEFWR6K6GGLaW`) from objectui#9472's diagnosis. ⛔ Not claimed, no assignee. ⛔ This card rules on nothing.

⚠️ **Routing declared, not assumed.** The triage seat objectstack#6015 is 🔴 vacant (shift-close brief 2026-09-14T05:50:56Z, no later marker), so this card is filed with a lane under the stand-in clause. `packages/components` is a **published library**, which objectui's three-stream rule sends to `domain:ui`. ⛔ The filing seat is `domain:devx` and is **not** claiming this — routing it away from itself. The incoming triage seat should re-read the lane; overturning costs nothing.

**Dedupe words:** `components index.css` · `source(none)` · `automatic source detection` · `CHANGELOG prose` · `published stylesheet`

## The defect

`packages/components/src/index.css` opens with a bare `@import 'tailwindcss';` and is the **only one of this repo's four stylesheet entries without `source(none)`** — `fields`, `plugin-grid` and `plugin-kanban` all carry it, and their own comments say why.

⇒ Tailwind v4 **automatic source detection** is ON for that entry, rooted at `packages/components/`, so it scans **every non-gitignored file under that directory** — including `CHANGELOG.md`, and including prose.

## Measured: 23 of the 1312 published utilities exist only because of prose

Compiling the `components` entry as-is versus with `source(none)`, same probe, same run:

| | classes |
|:--|--:|
| as shipped today | **1312** |
| with `source(none)` | **1289** |
| **difference** | **23 lost, 0 gained** |

⭐ The lost set is **visibly prose**: `bg-blue-500`, `hover:bg-blue-700`, `h-[600px]`, `md:text-2xl`, `text-white` — and **one token containing a typographic ellipsis**, which no real source file could contain. ⇒ these are not utilities anyone authored; they are sentences that happened to look like class names.

## ⭐ Why it is worse than 23 stray rules: it can SUBTRACT a rule another package needs

The plugin builders subtract whatever `components` already ships. So a class that appears in `components`' sheet **by accident** is removed from the plugin sheets **on purpose**.

Measured end to end on a real post-version tree (the real `pnpm changeset:version`, ⛔ not a simulation):

1. `.changeset/8506-detail-placeholders-shared-empty-value.md` names `@object-ui/components` and its body contains the literal text `text-muted-foreground/60 text-sm`.
2. `changeset:version` writes that body into `packages/components/CHANGELOG.md`.
3. That prose compiles `.text-muted-foreground\/60` into `components`' sheet.
4. `plugin-kanban`'s builder subtracts it ⇒ its published sheet **loses** the rule — while `packages/plugin-kanban/src/KanbanImpl.tsx:492` **still emits that class**.
5. ⇒ the plugin build **SUCCEEDS, no throw**: **59 classes → 58**, rule gone.

⇒ ⭐ **an under-styled published package with a green build** — exactly the defect the builder's own error text names. It would ship on the next release.

⚠️⚠️ **And the failure mode has a louder twin waiting.** `bg-card/60` **is** in `plugin-kanban`'s `MUST_SURVIVE` list (verified by ablation). ⇒ the day a changeset body happens to mention *that* class, the release build stops being silently wrong and **throws outright**. Today's silence is luck about which class got written into which changeset.

## Reproduction, with its controls

Ablation on `packages/components/CHANGELOG.md`, each leg proving the injection landed on disk (grep count before/after + `git hash-object` differing from the HEAD blob), each restored and verified by hash equality:

| leg | injected | result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **POS1** | `text-muted-foreground/60` | exit **1**, production assertion verbatim: `expected [ 'text-muted-foreground/60' ] to deeply equal []` |
| **NEG** | `zzz-not-a-tailwind-class-9472` — same file, same command | exit **0**, green ⇒ ⭐ it is **not** "any edit" |
| **POS2** | `bg-card/60` | exit **1** naming `.bg-card/60` ⇒ the mechanism is **general**, not one unlucky string |

**Reverse verification of the candidate fix:** with `source(none)` in force **and** the same injection that made POS1 red, the stylesheet test is exit **0**, green. ⇒ both directions measured.

## ⛔ Why the narrow fix is the wrong one — and this is on the record already

The tempting repair is `@source not '../CHANGELOG.md'`. ⛔ **Rejected on evidence, not taste:** objectui#8446 adjudicated this exact hazard family for this exact file, and its fix **enumerated the bad doors** (adding `@source not` exclusions for test directories) while leaving automatic detection **ON**. ⇒ `CHANGELOG.md` is simply the door that enumeration did not list. Adding one more exclusion repeats the move that already failed.

⇒ the candidate is the `source(none)` pin the three sibling entries already carry.

## ⚠️ What this card does NOT decide

- ⛔ **Whether losing those 23 published utilities is acceptable.** They are prose-derived and almost certainly nobody's intent, but they are **currently shipped bytes** of `@object-ui/components/dist/index.css`. That is a product call for the package's owner, and this card ⛔ does not take it.
- ⛔ Whether the fix needs a changeset and of what size — the filing seat does not own this package.
- ⛔ Anything about objectui#9472's release-lane red beyond naming this as the carrier of **48 of its 63** assertion annotations.

## Why this is filed rather than folded into objectui#9472

objectui#9472 is a `domain:devx` card about a **CI lane being red**. This is a **published-artifact defect in a UI package** that happens to be what that lane correctly objects to. Different lane, different owner, different risk. ⇒ ⛔ not a footnote on someone else's card.

Refs: objectui#9472 (the release-lane red this causes) · objectui#8446 (the earlier adjudication of this hazard family on this file).
